body: This is important to me since I write most of my code in the `const`/`let` style thanks to awesome @olov's [defs](https://www.npmjs.org/package/defs) project but still has to sometimes write sth using `var` so I cannot just enable `block-scoped-var`.

I think you may not understand the `block-scoped-var` rule. When you do use `var`, just place it at function or program level and you're good. escope should treat `const`/`let` like `var`, and `block-scoped-var` will ensure they're used only within their respective blocks.

@michaelficarra You're right it shouldn't break `var`. However, ESLint should understand how `const`/`let` scope works and not warn about redeclaring the variable when it's declared in two different blocks.

BTW, I have other problems with the `block-scoped-var` rule, see #919.
To be clear, your issue is with `no-redeclare` in this issue, no `block-scoped-var`.
Yes, sorry for the confusion. It was a side-comment that grew.
